page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. This KVM-hypervised instance features 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. A key hardware feature of this instance is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 959 GB SSD, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.i2.xlarge exhibits lower-tier performance characteristics across multiple dimensions. In CPU-intensive tasks, the instance registered weak results, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1102.28 and a multi-core score of 2922.29. Memory performance is similarly constrained; while small-block cached read bandwidth reached 163.34 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth dropped to a poor 19.71 GB/sec. Computational workloads such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also fell into the bottom decile of performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i2.xlarge trades raw processing speed and memory throughput for high local storage density and a generous memory-to-vCPU ratio. This makes it a viable option for workloads that require significant local storage capacity and moderate memory footprints but do not demand high-performance compute. Suitable workloads include local database hosting, basic file serving, and lightweight caching systems where storage capacity and memory capacity are prioritized over high-speed execution.
